q: 1. Pigments are available in the form of
explain: Pigments are typically supplied as fine powders, later mixed with a vehicle to form paint.

q: 2. The most important constituent of varnish, is
explain: Resin is the essential film-forming ingredient of varnish, giving it its glossy, protective finish.

q: 3. Plastic asphalt is
options: used as a water proofing layer over roof
a mixture of cement and asphalt
explain: Plastic asphalt, being flexible and impermeable, is applied as a waterproofing layer over roofs.

q: 4. The most fire resistant paint are
explain: Asbestos paints are the most fire resistant because asbestos itself is a non-combustible mineral fiber.

q: 5. The pigment used in paints for corrosive resistance, is
explain: Red lead is the standard anti-corrosive pigment used in primer paints, especially for iron and steel.

q: 6. The defect in painting caused by excessive moisture vaporizing in back to the film is known as
explain: Blistering occurs when trapped moisture vaporizes and pushes up the paint film from beneath, forming bubbles.

q: 7. A thinner used in distemper is
explain: Since distemper is a water-based paint, water itself is used as the thinner to adjust its consistency.

q: 8. A hydro-carbon material that completely soluble in carbon disulphide is known as
explain: Bitumen is a hydrocarbon material that is completely soluble in carbon disulphide, a key test for its purity/identification.

q: 9. The colour of asphalt is
options: deep black with slight tinge of redness
explain: Asphalt is generally described as black-brownish in color, distinguishing it visually from other bituminous materials.

q: 10. Coal-tar is obtained by destructive distillation of
explain: Coal-tar is a byproduct obtained from the destructive (high-temperature, air-free) distillation of coal.

q: 11. Bitumen felt is used for
explain: Bitumen felt is impermeable and flexible, making it ideal for waterproofing and damp-proofing applications.

q: 12. The standard width of asbestos cement sheet is
explain: Standard asbestos cement corrugated sheets are commonly manufactured with a width of about 1.23 m.

q: 13. Asphalt is a good insulator of
explain: Asphalt, being a dense hydrocarbon-mineral composite, insulates well against heat, sound, and electrical conduction.

q: 14. Regarding solubility of asphalt, it is soluble in
explain: Since asphalt contains inert mineral matter along with bitumen, it dissolves only partially in carbon disulphide, unlike pure bitumen.

q: 15. The specific gravity of bitumen is
explain: Bitumen typically has a specific gravity of around 1.0 to 1.09, slightly denser than water.

q: 16. Which of the following material exhibits plasticity?
explain: Copper, steel, and hot bitumen can all be deformed and reshaped without breaking, exhibiting plasticity under appropriate conditions.

q: 17. In paints, pigment is responsible for:
explain: Pigment is the solid coloring component in paint responsible for its color and opacity.

q: 18. Paints with white lead base are suitable for painting of
options: both wood work and iron work
explain: White lead based paints are best suited for wood work, as they adhere well and protect timber surfaces effectively.

q: 19. Linseed oil is rapidly soluble in
explain: Linseed oil readily dissolves in a range of common solvents including turpentine, naphtha, and alcohol.

q: 20. Lithophone is
options: an oxide of iron used as a base
explain: Lithopone is a white pigment composed of zinc sulfide and barium sulfate, used as an alternative to white lead.

q: 21. The basic purpose of a retarder in concrete is
options: to increase the initial setting time of cement paste in concrete
to decrease the initial setting time of cement paste in concrete
to render the concrete more water tight
to improve the workability of concrete mix
explain: A retarder is added specifically to extend (increase) the initial setting time, giving more working time before the concrete sets.

q: 22. The function of base of an oil paint is
options: to form the body of the paint
to reinforce the film of the paint after drying
to prevent penetration of paint to lower surfaces
explain: The 'base' (like white lead or zinc oxide) provides the bulk or body of the paint and determines its character.

q: 23. Base pigments are used for
explain: The base is a solid substance in a fine state of division and forms the bulk of a paint. It imparts durability and protects the surface from weathering.

q: 24. The commonly used thinner in distempers
explain: Distemper is a water-based paint, therefore water is used as the thinning agent to achieve the desired consistency.

q: 25. The defect in painting over a smooth and glossy surface due to which paint does not stick to the surface, is known as
explain: Blistering occurs when gas or moisture is trapped under the paint film, often because it fails to adhere to a smooth or glossy surface.

q: 26. Distemper is a mixture of
explain: Basic distemper consists of powdered chalk mixed with water and a binder (like glue/size).

q: 27. The oily liquid in which base and pigment are dissolved to form a paint is called
explain: The vehicle (or binder) is the liquid that holds the pigment and base in suspension and helps it adhere to the surface.

q: 28. The small areas on painted surface enclosed by hair line cracks are called
explain: Crazing refers to the formation of fine, shallow hairline cracks on the surface of the paint.

q: 29. Lacquer is
explain: Lacquers are technically a type of spirit varnish that dries by evaporation of the solvent.

q: 30. The best primer used for structural steel/iron is
explain: Red lead is the most effective primer for steel as it provides excellent corrosion resistance.

q: 31. Distemper paint means
explain: Distemper is fundamentally a water-based paint made from chalk, pigment, and a glue/water binder.

q: 32. Duco is the trade name for
explain: Duco is a well-known brand of cellulose-based paint commonly used in the automotive industry.

q: 33. The paints used in aircrafts are
explain: Cellulose paints (lacquers) are used for aircraft because they dry very rapidly by evaporation and provide a hard, smooth, and flexible surface.

q: 34. French polish is made by dissolving the resin
explain: French polish is a type of spirit varnish made by dissolving shellac in methylated spirit.

q: 35. PVC controls in paint
explain: Pigment Volume Concentration (PVC) affects nearly all physical properties of the paint film, including its sheen and strength.

q: 36. The cracks developed throughout thickness of paint due various reason is known as
explain: Cracking involves deep breaks in the paint film that often expose the underlying surface.

q: 37. The material generally not used as extender in paints is
explain: Zinc white is a primary pigment (base), whereas silica, gypsum, and talc are inert materials used as extenders.

q: 38. The radiator of vehicles are pointed with
explain: Bronze or aluminum paints are used for radiators due to their high thermal conductivity and heat resistance.

q: 39. Brilliant varnish is
explain: Spirit varnishes (like French polish) dry quickly to a very high, brilliant gloss.

q: 40. Bitumen paint renders
explain: Bituminous paints are primarily used for their excellent protective and anti-corrosive qualities on ironwork.

q: 41. Mastic asphalt is generally used for
explain: Due to its impermeable nature, mastic asphalt is a standard material for Damp Proof Courses (DPC) and waterproof layer  in buildings.

q: 42. Asphalt in obtained form
explain: Asphalt is the heavy residue left after the distillation of certain types of crude petroleum.

q: 43. The union of two or more smaller molecule of same or different types with or without elimination of water is known as
explain: Polymerization is the chemical process of combining small molecules (monomers) into a large network (polymer).

q: 44. The degradation of polymers by disrupting the inter molecular bond is known as
explain: Depolymerization is the reverse of polymerization, where the polymer is broken down into its original monomers or smaller fragments.

q: 45. Plastics are................materials.
explain: Plastics are organic polymers, primarily derived from petrochemicals (carbon-based).

q: 46. Distemper is used on
options: plastered surface not exposed to weather
explain: Distemper is a water-based interior finish that is not suitable for surfaces exposed to rain or sun.

q: 47. A good quality bitumen suitable for paving jobs should not indicated a loss in weight more than
explain: When heated, high-quality bitumen should be stable with minimal loss of volatile components (typically <1%).
